name: Hamilton Anxiety Rating Scale (HAM-A)
directions: Clinician-rated. Select one severity for each of 14 items based on the clinical interview. 0 not present, 1 mild, 2 moderate, 3 severe, 4 very severe.

questions.definition: Worries, anticipation of the worst, fearful anticipation, irritability.
Tension, fatigability, startle response, trembling, restlessness or inability to relax.
Fear of dark, strangers, being left alone, animals, traffic or crowds.
Difficulty falling asleep, broken/unsatisfying sleep, fatigue on waking, dreams or nightmares.
Loss of interest or pleasure, depression, early waking or diurnal swing.
Pains, aches, twitching, stiffness, jerks, teeth grinding or increased muscle tone.
Tinnitus, blurred vision, hot/cold flushes, weakness or prickling sensations.
Tachycardia, palpitations, chest pain, throbbing vessels or fainting feelings.
Chest pressure, choking feelings, sighing or dyspnoea.
Swallowing difficulty, abdominal symptoms, nausea, vomiting or bowel changes.
Urinary frequency/urgency or reproductive/sexual symptoms described in the source form.
Dry mouth, flushing, pallor, sweating, giddiness or tension headache.
Fidgeting, pacing, hand tremor, furrowed brow, sighing or rapid respiration.

attribution: Hamilton M. The assessment of anxiety states by rating. Br J Med Psychol. 1959;32:50–55. Supplied text identifies HAM-A as public domain.
